title: TrueNorth cached source
description: One document the question bank is written against, `content/sources/<id>.json`. ADR-0003 turns on a `sourceHash`: a verification status is granted for a hash, and when the hash changes the status stops matching and the claim falls out of the build without anyone noticing the edit. That only works if the hash, and what it is a hash of, are recorded somewhere a gate can read - which is this file. It is a register, not a copy: `licence` and `committed` exist because Discover Canada is Crown copyright and is paraphrased and cited rather than redistributed (ADR-0004).

id.description: The id a question's source block cites. Kebab-case, unique among sources.

edition.description: Which edition or revision this hash is of, in words. Two files can share a title and differ in every fact that matters.

file.description: The fetched document, relative to content/sources/. Present in the working tree only when `committed` is true.

extractedText.description: The plain-text extraction the verifier actually reads and quotes evidence from, relative to content/sources/. Kept beside the original because a hash of a PDF says nothing about whether the text came out of it intact.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of `file`. This is the hash a question's verification is granted against.

extractedTextSha256.description: SHA-256 of `extractedText`. Separate from `sha256` on purpose: a re-extraction with a different tool changes what the verifier read without changing the source document, and that is a difference the bank must be able to see. Every question's `source.sourceHash` is this digest, so `extraction` below - how the bytes it covers were produced - is what decides whether an outsider can check a single one of them.

extraction.description: How `extractedText` was produced from `file`, precisely enough for someone who has only the URL to regenerate the same bytes. Required whenever there is an extraction, because without it the digest above is a number nobody outside this machine can reproduce: a contributor can download the correct document, match its `sha256`, and still be unable to run the verbatim check, the quote-contiguity check or the evidence check, all of which read the extraction and not the document (ADR-0003 says a claim about a source must be re-derivable from the cached bytes). The recorded form carries the tool, its version and the exact command; the unrecorded form exists so that an extraction whose command was never written down declares that fact instead of looking like one nobody has filled in yet - the same reason `committed` is required rather than inferred from a missing file.

pages.description: Page count, when the source is paginated. A chapter's `page` is an offset into this.

retrievedAt.description: The date the file was fetched, YYYY-MM-DD. A date, not an instant: the fetch time of day carries no meaning and inviting one invites a fabricated one.

licence.description: Free text, not the credits enum: this is a document the project reads, never an asset it ships, so ADR-0004's redistribution test does not apply and a licence id would misrepresent Crown copyright.

committed.description: Is the file itself in this repository? False for anything the project may cite but not redistribute. When false, the hashes are the whole of the record and a verifier must re-fetch to check them.

chapters.description: The table of contents, so a question's `source.chapter` can be checked against something rather than trusted.

grainNote.description: Why this register's staleness flags are located the way they are, in the register's own words. Prose for the next person to add a flag, kept beside the flags rather than in an ADR because it is about this document rather than about the rule.

knownStaleness.description: What is already known to be out of date in this document, recorded before a question is written against it rather than discovered after one ships. A cached source is a snapshot of a page that keeps moving; this is the list of places the snapshot is known to lie.

liveChecks.description: The record of going to the LIVE page and comparing it with this cache. A different question from `knownStaleness`, and the two are easy to confuse. `knownStaleness` says *this cached text is wrong*; a live check says *we looked, and here is whether the wrongness is ours or theirs*. That distinction decides what a periodic re-check can possibly achieve. If the live page has moved on and the cache has not, re-fetching resolves the claim - which is the model this register was built on. If the live page states the same out-of-date thing the cache does, the source itself is unrevised: `sourceHash` keeps matching indefinitely, no drift-based quarantine can ever trigger, and re-fetching returns the same wrong text forever. Nothing else here can tell those two situations apart, and until this array existed nothing recorded which one we were in (ADR-0016).

allOf.$comment: An extraction with no record of how it was made pins the whole question bank to a digest only its author can regenerate. Saying `unrecorded` is allowed; saying nothing is not. Only property names this object already declares appear here (ADR-0007).

recordedExtraction.title: Recorded extraction
recordedExtraction.description: The tool, the version and the command that turn `file` into `extractedText`. `make sources` runs this command and compares the result with `extractedTextSha256`, so it is checked rather than described.

tool.description: The program, named the way a reader would install it - "pdftotext (poppler-utils)", not "a PDF extractor".

version.description: The version the recorded digest was produced with, exactly as the tool reports it. Text extraction is not stable across major versions of any extractor, so a digest with no version behind it is only half a record: when a re-run disagrees, this is the first thing to compare.

versionCommand.description: How to ask the tool for that version, when it is not `<tool> --version`. `make sources` runs it and reports a mismatch, which is the difference between "your extractor is newer than ours" and "the source moved".

command.description: The exact command, run from the repository root, that reads `file` and writes the extraction to STDOUT. Stdout rather than a path so that a re-run can be hashed and compared without overwriting the working copy, and so that a command cannot quietly write somewhere else: `make sources` refuses one containing an output redirection, a command separator or a substitution, and runs what is left through `sh -c`. A pipeline is fine.

reproducedAt.description: The date this command was last run and did produce `extractedTextSha256`, YYYY-MM-DD. A recorded command nobody has re-run is a claim; this is the date it was last a measurement.

unrecordedExtraction.title: Unrecorded extraction
unrecordedExtraction.description: The extraction exists and how it was made was not written down. A declared absence, not a gap: it keeps "nobody recorded this" distinguishable from "this register predates the field", it makes the count of irreproducible sources something `make sources` can print, and it cannot be reached by omission, because the schema requires an `extraction` of one form or the other. Replacing it with a recorded form is a matter of finding a command whose output hashes to `extractedTextSha256` - and if no command does, that is a finding about the corpus and belongs in `reason` rather than in a re-hashed register.

reason.description: What is known about how the extraction was made, and what has already been tried and did not reproduce it. Written for the next person to attempt it, so they do not repeat the same two experiments.

sourceChapter.title: Source chapter
sourceChapter.$comment: There is deliberately NO `level` property here. One existed, described as "which of the ten levels teaches this chapter", it had no caller, and it was false: eleven `government` questions (level 4) cite the Federal Elections chapter (level 5) and interleave with `elections` questions on pages 60, 62 and 66. A subject is a teaching remit and a chapter is where the sentences are; the relation is many-to-many and the unit of exclusive claim is the proposition, identified by a question's `source.quote` and checked in `tests/unit/contracts/a-proposition-belongs-to-one-subject.test.ts`. See ADR-0028. `additionalProperties: false` below is what stops the field coming back.

title.description: The heading exactly as it appears in the source. A question's source.chapter must match one of these.

endPage.description: Last page of the chapter, inclusive. Without it a chapter is only a START marker and every page after it belongs to the previous chapter by accident - which is how 27 questions from pp. 60-69 came to cite `Federal Elections`, mechanically correct and wrong at a glance. An explicit range is what lets a question's `source.page` be checked against the chapter it claims.

knownStaleness.title: Known staleness
knownStaleness.description: One thing this snapshot is known to get wrong, the chapters it touches, and what an author must do instead. `action` is instructions to the author and the verifier, not a machine directive: a question in an affected chapter is expected to be marked volatile and verified against the live page, and no gate can tell whether it was. `upstream` and `bannedFromAnswers` were added by ADR-0016, after a live check established that the official source is itself unrevised. When the publisher will never correct a flag, re-verifying against an unchanged page is a recurring cost with no possible finding, and routing the answers around the stale fact is the only mitigation that can work - so it is recorded and checked instead of left to an author's unstated judgement.

grain.description: How precisely the stale region is located. `pages` means the claims sit on the pages listed below and only a question citing one of them is affected; `chapter` means the whole of every chapter in `affects` is suspect. Prefer `pages`. A flag at chapter grain over a long chapter forces every question in it volatile, and a flag that fires on everything carries the same information as a flag that fires on nothing - the verifier can no longer use it to prioritise, which is what it was for.

pages.description: The pages the stale claims are on. Required when `grain` is `pages`; a page here must fall inside one of the chapters named in `affects`, or the flag localises to somewhere no question can cite.

upstream.description: Will a future edition of the source fix this, on the evidence of `liveChecks`? `revises` means the publisher maintains this document, so the flag eventually clears by re-fetching and the existing rule is right. `does-not-revise` means the live page has been checked and states the same out-of-date thing: the flag will not clear by waiting, the periodic re-check has nothing to find, and the mitigation has to move into the questions - which is why `bannedFromAnswers` becomes required. `unknown` is the honest answer before anyone has looked, and the re-check rule treats it exactly as `revises`, because continuing to fetch is the safe direction. Absent means `unknown`; the field is optional so that a register written before it existed stays valid, not so the question can be dodged.

bannedFromAnswers.description: Terms that must not appear in any option or explanation of a question citing an affected region. This is the mitigation that actually works when the source will never be corrected, and until this field existed it was an author's unrecorded judgement - correct, invisible, and enforced by nothing. Listed as terms rather than described in prose so a gate can search for them (ADR-0016), matched case-insensitively as whole words against the EN and FR text a player reads. List the specific stale tokens - "Her Majesty", "Elizabeth", "53 other nations", "308" - not the topic. A list that over-fires costs one build failure and a refined entry; a list that under-fires ships the wrong fact to somebody studying for a citizenship test.

allOf.$comment: Page grain without pages is chapter grain wearing a more precise name. Only property names this object already declares appear here (ADR-0007).

Declaring that the source will never correct a flag is declaring that the only remaining mitigation lives in the answers - so say what the answers may not depend on. A `does-not-revise` with no term list switches the periodic re-check off and puts nothing in its place, which is strictly worse than the busywork it replaces. Only property names this object already declares appear here (ADR-0007).

liveCheck.title: Live source check
liveCheck.description: One occasion on which the live page was fetched and compared with this cache. Kept as a list rather than one latest reading, because the pattern across checks is the evidence: `source-unrevised` after a single look is a guess, and after three looks spanning a year it is a finding. Overwriting would destroy exactly the signal that justifies moving a question off per-run re-verification.

checkedAt.description: The date the live page was fetched, YYYY-MM-DD. This is OUR clock, and it is deliberately a separate field from `pages[].sourceDateModified`, which is the page's claim about itself. The gap between the two is the whole finding.

checkedBy.description: Which agent or model performed the fetch and the comparison. ADR-0003 separates author from verifier; a check nobody is named for is a check nobody can be asked about.

pages.description: One entry per live URL compared. A source with several chapters lives at several URLs and they are revised independently, so a single verdict for the whole source would average unrelated facts.

finding.description: What the comparison established, as a value a gate branches on rather than prose a person interprets. `source-revised`: the live page has moved on and this cache is behind it, so re-fetch, re-hash and re-verify. `source-unrevised`: the live page states the same out-of-date thing, so the staleness is upstream and permanent until the publisher acts. `source-withdrawn`: the page is gone. `source-unreachable`: the fetch failed. The last two are separate on purpose and folding them would be the defect - a 500 or a DNS failure is not a retraction, and treating one as the other would let a transient network fault read as the Government of Canada removing a document. Same reasoning as ADR-0009's split of DISCHARGED from VOIDED.

consequence.description: What was done about the finding, in the checker's own words: which questions were re-verified, quarantined, or deliberately left alone, and why. The counterpart to a staleness flag's `action` - that one is instructions before the fact, this one is what actually happened.

liveCheckPage.title: Live check page
liveCheckPage.description: One live URL, compared against this cache on one occasion.

url.description: The live URL fetched. Chapter-level, not the source's landing page: the landing page is what the register's root `url` records, and it can be perfectly current while the chapter under it is nine years old.

chapter.description: Which chapter this URL carries. Must match one of this register's `chapters[].title`, so a live check binds to the same vocabulary a question's `source.chapter` uses and the two can be joined. Checked by tests/unit/contracts/questions-cite-a-cached-source.test.ts, because JSON Schema cannot compare a value against a sibling array.

sourceDateModified.description: The date the page states about ITSELF - canada.ca's "Date modified" - or null when it publishes none. Null is a real answer and the field is required rather than optional, so "the page carries no date" stays distinguishable from "nobody recorded one". It is the page's claim and not a fact: a page can be edited without the stamp moving, and a stamp can move on a navigation change. It is the cheapest available evidence that a document is unmaintained, not proof that it is.

agreesWithCache.description: Did the live text agree with our extraction on every claim in `claimsCompared`? True is the reading that inverts this register's model: it means a re-fetch would change nothing, and `sourceHash` will go on matching a document that is wrong.

claimsCompared.description: The specific claims compared, one per string. Required and non-empty because "textually identical" is unfalsifiable without saying identical ON WHAT - two documents differ somewhere - and a verdict with no stated scope is the vacuum this project keeps closing. These are the sentences a later checker repeats to reproduce the finding.
